output.summary: KEP-4176 proposes a new CPUManager static policy option, `distribute-cpus-across-cores`, that prefers allocating CPUs from different physical cores on the same socket. The KEP status is implementable at stage alpha.
output.rationale: Workloads that get two hyperthreads of one physical core can suffer cache and noisy-neighbor effects, so the option spreads allocations across cores while still using the L2 cache on one socket. Reviewers agreed the change is small and self-contained, and the option was approved after the KEP freeze deadline was missed due to reviewer bandwidth. Reviewers required that the option's interaction with existing options (notably full-pcpus-only and distribute-cpus-across-numa) be documented before alpha.

alternatives.option: Add a new CPU manager policy instead of a policy option
alternatives.why_not: A reviewer stated that it should be a policy option instead of a new one, and later clarified it is a new option, so existing feature gates are good enough.

alternatives.option: Use NRI resource policy (Balloons, preferSpreadOnPhysicalCores) instead of changing the kubelet
alternatives.why_not: Maintainers said the NRI plugins do not replicate the static policy 1:1 and the approach differs from the static policy; the reviewer said either approach could move forward, but they were in favor of changing cpumanager.

alternatives.option: Make the option error out or implicitly switch behavior when combined with full-pcpus-only
alternatives.why_not: A reviewer preferred treating the combination as a misconfiguration (error) for predictability, but the sources do not record a final decision on this; interaction was left as an open item.

evidence.quote: We propose to add a new `CPUManager` policy option called `distribute-cpus-across-cores` to the static CPUManager policy.
@klueska I accepted the change and I think that's makes it more clear.
It will move from being a `CPUManagerPolicyAlphaOption` to a `CPUManagerPolicyBetaOption` to not having a feature gate protecting it at all.
Please file an exception request for this feature, as per the insructions here
For alpha, we may just call it incompatible with everything else (but it will be much much nicer to have it elaborated), but past alpha we need a proper exploration here.
